lessons.title: Quran & Seerah
lessons.subtitle: Revelation and the life of the Prophet (PBUH)

questions.prompt: Over what period was the Holy Quran revealed?
questions.explanation: About 23 years - roughly 13 years in Makkah and 10 in Madinah.

questions.prompt: The first revelation was received by the Prophet (PBUH) in the cave of:
questions.explanation: In the cave of Hira on Jabal-al-Noor; the first verses were of Surah Al-Alaq.

questions.prompt: How many Surahs are there in the Holy Quran?
questions.explanation: 114 Surahs, containing 30 Paras (Juz).

questions.prompt: Which is the longest Surah of the Holy Quran?
questions.explanation: Surah Al-Baqarah, with 286 verses. The shortest is Surah Al-Kawthar.

questions.prompt: The migration (Hijrah) to Madinah took place in:
questions.explanation: 622 CE, the year from which the Islamic Hijri calendar is counted.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Badr was fought in:
questions.explanation: 2 AH (624 CE) - the first major battle, in which a small Muslim force defeated the Quraysh.

questions.prompt: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was concluded in:
questions.explanation: 6 AH (628 CE); though its terms seemed unfavourable, the Quran called it a clear victory.

lessons.title: Pillars & Hadith
lessons.subtitle: Worship, obligations and the Hadith collections

questions.prompt: How many pillars of Islam are there?
questions.explanation: Shahadah, Salah, Zakat, Sawm and Hajj.

questions.prompt: The standard rate of Zakat on accumulated wealth is:
questions.explanation: 2.5% of wealth above the nisab that has been held for a full lunar year. 'Ushr' on produce is 5% or 10%.

questions.prompt: Fasting in the month of Ramadan was made obligatory in:
questions.explanation: 2 AH, in the same year as the change of Qibla and the Battle of Badr.

questions.prompt: In Sunni tradition, the most authentic collection of Hadith is:
questions.explanation: Sahih al-Bukhari, compiled by Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari, followed by Sahih Muslim.

questions.prompt: The Qibla was changed from Bait-ul-Maqdis to the Kaaba in:
questions.explanation: 2 AH in Madinah, as recorded in Surah Al-Baqarah.

questions.prompt: Hajj is obligatory on a Muslim who can afford it:
questions.explanation: Once in a lifetime for those with the physical and financial means; further pilgrimages are voluntary.

questions.prompt: How many obligatory (fard) prayers are prescribed each day?
questions.explanation: Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

lessons.title: Caliphate & History
lessons.subtitle: The rightly guided caliphs and after

questions.prompt: The first Caliph of Islam was:
questions.explanation: Hazrat Abu Bakr Siddique (RA), who led the Muslim community from 632 to 634 CE.

questions.prompt: Standard copies of the Quran were prepared and distributed during the caliphate of:
questions.explanation: Hazrat Usman (RA) had standard copies sent to the provinces, which is why he is titled Jami-ul-Quran.

questions.prompt: Which caliph is known by the title 'Farooq'?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) - 'the one who distinguishes truth from falsehood'.

questions.prompt: The Battle of Karbala took place in:
questions.explanation: 61 AH (680 CE), where Hazrat Imam Hussain (RA) and his companions were martyred.

questions.prompt: The capital of the Umayyad Caliphate was:
questions.explanation: Damascus in Syria, from 661 CE until the Abbasid takeover in 750 CE.

questions.prompt: The Abbasid Caliphate ruled from its capital at:
questions.explanation: Baghdad, founded in 762 CE by Caliph Al-Mansur and a centre of learning for centuries.

questions.prompt: Which companion was given the title 'Saif-ullah' (the Sword of Allah)?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Khalid bin Waleed (RA), commander in the Ridda wars and the conquests of Iraq and Syria.
